titleEn: Bathroom Plumbing in Vancouver Renovations 2026: What Homeowners Actually Pay and How It Works
titleZh: 温哥华浴室装修管道2026：业主实际费用及完整流程
excerptEn: A complete breakdown of bathroom plumbing costs in Greater Vancouver 2026 — rough-in, re-piping, water heater, permits and how the work fits into your renovation timeline.
excerptZh: 大温哥华2026年浴室管道费用完整解析——包括管道预装、改管、热水器、许可证费用及施工流程。
contentEn:
In Greater Vancouver bathroom renovations, plumbing typically runs $2,500-$18,000 depending on scope. A simple vanity replacement costs $2,500-$5,000. Moving a toilet or adding a second sink can push costs to $8,000-$18,000. These numbers come from real Reno Stars project invoices across Richmond, Vancouver, North Vancouver and Burnaby in 2025-2026.

How Much Does Bathroom Plumbing Cost in Vancouver and BC?

The total depends on what you are starting with and what you want to change. Here is what Reno Stars sees most commonly across bathroom renovation projects in the Lower Mainland:

Work TypeCost Range (CAD)
Vanity drain/connect (no wall work)$800-$1,800
Replace faucet, shower valve, drain$1,500-$3,500
Rough-in for new bathroom (no finish)$3,000-$6,000
Full re-pipe (copper or PEX)$4,500-$12,000
Water heater replacement (tank)$1,500-$3,500
Tankless water heater install$4,000-$8,000
Shower pan + linear drain$1,200-$2,800
Sump pump / backwater valve$1,800-$3,500

Costs vary by city. Richmond and Burnaby tend to be slightly lower than West Vancouver due to permit fee structures. All prices include materials and labour.

Do You Need a Plumber in BC?

Yes — any work that connects to the potable water supply, drain-waste-vent (DWV) system, or natural gas line in BC must be performed or inspected by a licensed plumber. Homeowners can do minor cosmetic replacement of faucets and showerheads themselves in BC, but anything involving soldering, drain modification, or gas lines requires a licensed contractor. A Reno Stars project manager coordinates licensed plumbers as part of every bathroom renovation.

What Permits Are Required?

For bathroom plumbing in Greater Vancouver, the permit situation depends on your municipality:

  • Vancouver: Plumbing permit required for any drain-waste-vent modification. $150-$300 per fixture alteration.
  • Richmond / Burnaby / Coquitlam: Plumbing permit required for new rough-in or relocation. $100-$250 per fixture.
  • North Vancouver / West Vancouver: Plumbing permit plus a building permit if walls are opened. Combined fees typically $300-$600.
  • Delta / Surrey: Separate plumbing and building permits. Fees vary by number of fixtures.

Reno Stars handles all permit applications as part of the project management fee. Homeowners do not need to apply separately.

How Plumbing Fits Into the Renovation Timeline

Plumbing is sequenced in a specific order within a bathroom renovation. Getting the sequence right prevents costly rework:

  1. Demolition (days 1-3): Remove finishes, expose existing pipes. No plumber needed yet.
  2. Plumbing rough-in (days 3-7): Licensed plumber runs new copper or PEX supply lines and DWV connections before insulation and drywall. This is the only time plumbing can be modified without destroying finished walls.
  3. Electrical rough-in (same days 3-7): Electrician and plumber coordinate — do not let one cover the other's work before inspection.
  4. Inspection (day 7-10): City inspector reviews plumbing and electrical rough-in. This must pass before insulation and drywall.
  5. Insulation + vapour barrier (days 10-14)
  6. Drywall (days 14-18)
  7. Plumbing finish work (days 18-22): Faucet, shower trim, toilet, vanity plumbing connections — plumber returns after walls are closed.
  8. Final inspection (day 22-25)

Total timeline for a full bathroom renovation in Greater Vancouver: 4-8 weeks depending on scope and permit queue times. Cities with busier permit offices (Vancouver, North Vancouver) can add 1-2 weeks to the schedule.

Common Mistakes Homeowners Make With Bathroom Plumbing

  • Moving fixtures without understanding soil stack constraints. In Richmond and Delta, soil stack locations often constrain where toilets can be relocated. Moving a toilet more than 3 feet from the existing stack may require cutting the concrete slab and a larger permit.
  • Forgetting about the backwater valve. The City of Vancouver requires a backwater valve on any new bathroom below street level. This adds $1,500-$2,500 and must be permitted separately.
  • Choosing a tankless heater without assessing gas line capacity. Many Vancouver homes built before 1990 have 3/4-inch gas lines. A tankless heater may need a 1-inch upgrade ($1,200-$3,000 extra).
  • Not pressure-testing before closing walls. Reno Stars always pressure-tests at 80 PSI for 30 minutes before insulation. Leaks found after drywall are 10x the cost to fix.

Planning a bathroom renovation in the Lower Mainland? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars. Our team of licensed plumbers and carpenters covers Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, North Vancouver, Coquitlam, Delta, Surrey and surrounding areas.

Real Project Examples

Reno Stars has completed dozens of bathroom renovations across Greater Vancouver. Here are three that involved significant plumbing work:

One Richmond ensuite project required moving the toilet 4 feet across the slab — the plumber installed a new cast-iron drain line through the concrete, with a backwater valve installed per City of Richmond requirements. The project took 6 weeks and all plumbing passed inspection first time. See the full project at /en/projects/ensuite-bathroom-renovation-richmond/.

A West Vancouver luxury bathroom project included a curbless European-style shower pan, a bench, body jets, and a rain head. The plumber ran 60 feet of PEX supply line and a new 2-inch DWV line for the linear drain. See the full project at /en/projects/west-vancouver-luxury-bathroom-champagne-gold/.

A North Vancouver herringbone tile bathroom included full re-piping of the bathroom section in PEX, a new pressure-balancing shower valve, and a frameless glass enclosure. Reno Stars coordinated the plumber and tiler on overlapping schedules. See the full project at /en/projects/north-vancouver-bathroom-renovation-herringbone-tile/.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does bathroom plumbing last in a Vancouver home?

Copper supply lines in Greater Vancouver homes typically last 40-60 years. PEX lines installed since 2005 have a similar or longer lifespan and are now the standard in new BC construction. Drain lines in cast iron last 50-80 years; PVC drain lines can last indefinitely.

Can I renovate a bathroom without moving plumbing?

Yes — keeping fixtures in their existing locations is the most cost-effective approach. A like-for-like replacement of a toilet, vanity, and faucet without moving supply or drain lines typically costs $3,000-$7,000 total and requires minimal permits.

Does insurance cover plumbing damage during renovation?

Standard homeowner's insurance in BC covers sudden, accidental damage (a burst pipe while work is underway) but does not cover damage from negligence or work done without required permits. Reno Stars carries $5-million liability coverage and obtains all required permits before work begins.

What is the most expensive plumbing item in a bathroom renovation?

Moving a toilet or adding a second full bathroom is typically the most expensive plumbing item — $4,000-$18,000 depending on whether concrete must be cut and whether the soil stack requires relocation. New shower pans and tankless water heaters are the next most expensive items.

Do I need a separate plumbing permit or is it part of the building permit?

In most Lower Mainland municipalities, a building permit covers the plumbing rough-in if it is filed together with the renovation scope. Vancouver and North Vancouver require separate plumbing permits for fixture alterations. Reno Stars files both as part of the standard project management process.
contentZh:
在大温哥华地区的浴室装修中，管道工程费用通常在 $2,500 至 $18,000 加元之间，具体取决于工程范围。简单地更换浴室柜人工费用约 $2,500 至 $5,000。移动马桶或增加第二个洗手池，费用可攀升至 $8,000 至 $18,000。这些数据来源于 Reno Stars 2025 至 2026 年在列治文、温哥华、北温及本拿比等地的真实工程发票。

大温哥华和BC省浴室管道费用是多少？

总费用取决于现有条件及您的改造需求。以下是 Reno Stars 在大温地区最常见的浴室装修项目费用明细：

工程类型费用范围（加元）
浴室柜排水/连接（无需墙面工程）$800-$1,800
更换龙头、淋浴阀、排水管$1,500-$3,500
新浴室管道预装（毛坯状态）$3,000-$6,000
全屋改管（铜管或PEX管）$4,500-$12,000
热水器更换（储水式）$1,500-$3,500
即热式热水器安装$4,000-$8,000
淋浴底盘 + 线性地漏$1,200-$2,800
排水泵 / 止回阀$1,800-$3,500

费用因城市而异。列治文和本拿比的 permit 费用结构略低于西温，原因是各城市政府收费不同。

BC省是否需要水管工？

是的——在BC省，任何涉及饮用水供水系统、排水排气管（DWV）系统或天然气管道的工程，必须由持牌水管工进行或接受检验。业主可自行更换水龙头和花洒等装饰性部件，但涉及焊接、排水改造或燃气管道的工作必须由持证承包商完成。Reno Stars 的项目经理会协调持牌水管工，作为每个浴室装修项目的标准流程。

需要哪些许可证？

大温哥华地区浴室管道的许可证要求因城市而异：

  • 温哥华：任何排水排气管道的改造均需 plumbing permit，每个装置改动费用约 $150-$300。
  • 列治文 / 本拿比 / 高贵林：新装或移位工程需 plumbing permit，每个装置费用约 $100-$250。
  • 北温 / 西温：Plumbing permit 加建筑 permit（若需打开墙面）。两项合并费用通常为 $300-$600。
  • Delta / Surrey：单独的 plumbing 和建筑 permit，费用按装置数量计算。

Reno Stars 代为办理所有许可证申请，包含在项目管理费用内，业主无需单独申请。

管道工程如何融入装修时间线

管道工程在浴室装修中按特定顺序进行。正确的顺序可避免高昂的返工成本：

  1. 拆除（第1-3天）：拆除装饰层，暴露现有管道。此阶段无需水管工。
  2. 管道预装（第3-7天）：持牌水管工在隔热和石膏板之前铺设新的铜管或 PEX 供水管及 DWV 管道连接。这是唯一可以在不破坏已完工墙面的情况下修改管道的时机。
  3. 电路预装（同期第3-7天）：电工和水管工需协调——一方不得在另一方验收前覆盖其工作。
  4. 检验（第7-10天）：市府检验员审查管道和电路预装。此阶段必须通过验收才能进行隔热和石膏板工程。
  5. 隔热 + 防潮层（第10-14天）
  6. 石膏板（第14-18天）
  7. 管道收尾工程（第18-22天）：水龙头、淋浴配件，马桶、浴室柜管道连接——水管工在墙面封闭后再次进场。
  8. 最终检验（第22-25天）

大温哥华地区全套浴室装修的总工期：4至8周，具体取决于工程范围及 permit 排队时间。温哥华和北温等 permit 办理量较大的城市，工期可能延长1至2周。

业主常犯的管道工程错误

  • 移动管道前未了解排水立管限制。在列治文和 Delta，排水立管的位置往往限制了马桶可以移动的范围。马桶移位超过现有立管3英尺可能需要切割混凝土楼板，并需要更大范围的 permit。
  • 忽略止回阀（backwater valve）。温哥华市要求所有位于街道标高以下的浴室必须安装止回阀。这项工程额外增加 $1,500-$2,500，且需单独申请 permit。
  • 选择即热式热水器前未评估燃气管道容量。许多1990年前建成的温哥华住宅使用3/4英寸燃气管道。即热式热水器可能需要升级至1英寸管道（额外 $1,200-$3,000）。
  • 封闭墙面前未进行压力测试。Reno Stars 在隔热前始终以 80 PSI 进行30分钟压力测试。石膏板封闭后发现漏水，修复成本是预防成本的10倍。

在大温地区规划浴室装修？获取 Reno Stars 的免费、无义务报价。我们的持牌水管工和木匠团队服务温哥华、列治文、本拿比、北温、高贵林、Delta、Surrey 及周边地区。

真实工程案例

Reno Stars 已在大温地区完成数十个浴室装修项目。以下三个案例均涉及重大管道工程：

列治文一个主卧浴室项目需要将马桶移动4英尺——水管工切割混凝土楼板安装了新的铸铁排水管，并按照列治文市要求安装了止回阀。该项目历时6周，所有管道工程一次通过验收。

西温一个豪华浴室项目包含无障碍欧式淋浴底盘、一个座位、按摩喷头和雨淋花洒。水管工铺设了60英尺 PEX 供水管和一条新的2英寸 DWV 管道用于线性地漏。最终交付符合温哥华"原地养老"标准的无障碍淋浴空间。

北温一个鱼骨砖铺贴浴室包含浴室区域的 PEX 全屋改管、一个新的压力平衡淋浴阀和无框玻璃隔断。Reno Stars 协调水管工和瓦工在重叠的时间表内施工，确保项目按时完成。

常见问题

温哥华住宅的浴室管道通常能用多少年？

大温哥华住宅的铜供水管通常使用寿命为40至60年。2005年以来安装的 PEX 管使用寿命相似或更长，现已成为BC省新建筑的标准做法。铸铁排水管使用寿命为50至80年；PVC 排水管可永久使用。

不移动管道可以装修浴室吗？

可以——将固定设施保留在原有位置是最经济的选择。在不移动供水或排水管道的情况下，更换马桶、浴室柜和水龙头的类似替换工程通常总费用为 $3,000 至 $7,000，所需的 permit 也最少。

装修期间的管道损坏保险是否覆盖？

BC省的标准业主保险覆盖突发、意外的损坏（工程进行中发生的爆管)，但不覆盖因疏忽或未申请所需 permit 而造成的损坏。Reno Stars 持有 $500 万责任险，并在开工前办理所有必需的 permit。

浴室装修中最昂贵的管道工程是什么？

移动马桶或增设第二个全功能浴室通常是费用最高的管道工程——根据是否需要切割混凝土楼板以及排水立管是否需要移位，费用在 $4,000 至 $18,000 之间。新的淋浴底盘和即热式热水器是仅次于马桶的第二高费用项目。

我需要单独的管道 permit 还是它包含在建筑 permit 中？

在大温地区大多数城市，如果建筑 permit 与装修范围一并提交，通常涵盖管道预装工程。温哥华和北温要求装置改造需单独的 plumbing permit。Reno Stars 会作为标准项目管理流程的一部分同时提交两类申请。
